_policy: Advisory, not scope. Nothing reads this file to change what the coverage gate
counts -- editing 'sources' or 'exclude' in the coverage config is a decision
the user makes deliberately, and a tool that did it silently would be shrinking
the denominator to flatter the number.
Verdicts: A testable as-is, B needs refactoring first, C not worth testing.
C is a real answer, not a failure. Tests over generated tables, empty
destructors and branchless accessors cannot fail for any reason worth knowing,
and a queue full of them costs review time while catching nothing.
Before writing C, answer: what bug would a test here catch that the compiler or
a downstream test would not? If there is an answer, it is not a C.
set_by 'rule' is recomputed on every run. set_by 'human' is preserved, and
keeps rule_would_say when the rules disagree, so drift shows up in the diff.

entries.name: impCubeTables::nextedge(int, int)
entries.reason: The one uncovered region is the fallback return(-1) on line 64, unreachable by construction: nextedge is private, called only from makeTriStripPatterns, and every call site derives currentedge from the same ec[]/vc[] topology tables nextedge itself walks, so the argument is always one of the three edges vc[vertex] lists. The other 9 regions are already exercised by the tables() tests. Reaching the fallback would need either an invalid (vertex, edge) pair the class invariants never produce, or a header edit to expose the method. Reached independently during the second /coverage-loop run (ss-44s) by the writer covering test_cubetables.cpp, and recorded here to match helios' identical verdict on the identical shared-core function -- the twins should not disagree about the same code.

entries.name: impSurface::addTriStripLength(unsigned char)
entries.reason: Still B, and now for the third distinct reason in this entry's history -- worth stating plainly because the first two are both gone. It is not GL-coupled (ss-aio de-GL'd the constructor) and it is not unobservable in principle (ss-or3 added accessors). It is dead in this build configuration: USE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS is 0, so draw() and polygonize never call it, and nothing reads triStripLengths or num_tristrips. Testing it means either an accessor for those two members or flipping the build flag, and the flag is a decision the Metal port should make rather than a test. Deliberately NOT marked C: a port that enables triangle strips makes this live code, and C would hide it.
